· Cause of death: hypothermia. Cold burns on the knees and hands; abrasions from metal on the fingertips.
· A small swelling on the skull at the back of the neck: a fall or a light blow; not enough to cause loss of consciousness.
· Time of death: 01.00–03.00.
AUTOPSY REPORT

Enzo Ferraro’s car (with the branch chief’s approval):

· In the glovebox, the cold room’s chrome inside handle, removed, two screws and a flat screwdriver; flour and the victim’s fingerprint on the handle.
· In the boot, the victim’s apron.
· On his phone, 6 October 00.04, a message to the contact ‘R.’: ‘Done. Let the flour come Monday.’

COLD ROOM EXAMINATION
The handle was already broken

Where did the cold room’s inside handle go?

Partner.
The bakery’s mine too; don’t forget that.
No.

I hit him once on the back of the neck; he just went down. I carried him into the cold room, took the handle off, turned the thermostat. I was going to find him in the morning; we’d say heart. Rocco said, ‘If Ciro doesn’t go, you go.’ I couldn’t throw the handle away. He was my sister’s husband.
A debt, yes. To Rocco. Ciro refused to pay, refused the flour, refused me.
You took the handle off.
At 23.30, together with Lucia. Ciro was inside; he said ‘I’ll close up.’ He did that every night.
He folds his floury arms across his chest.
When did you leave the shop last night?
I lowered the shutter; Ciro was inside, I left it halfway so he could close it himself. Then… I don’t remember locking it.

The handle hadn’t been thrown away.
The death was deemed an accident; a month later the shop switched to Caruso flour.
Enzo Ferraro was arrested. The ‘let the flour come Monday’ message and the Caruso flour deliveries were added to the file.

A ledger found under the till, kept in Ciro Amato’s handwriting:

· Eleven withdrawals from the till marked ‘E.’ in the last three months, totalling €9,400.
· On the last page: ‘Enzo — owes Rocco 12,000. Wiped if the flour comes from Caruso. NEVER.’ A heavy line beneath it.

Waitress.

At 23.30. Ciro was in the kitchen preparing the dough for tomorrow. Enzo was there too; the two of them were arguing over the ledger in the till. Enzo said, ‘If we talk to Rocco it all goes away,’ and Ciro said, ‘That flour never comes into my shop again.’ I left.
She winds her apron string round her finger.

Moussa Diop left by the morning train for Milano, for seasonal work. His number is switched off.

Ciro closes up himself every night, singing. Last night there was no singing. A big man in an apron lowered the shutter halfway, went in, came out alone ten minutes later, locked it. Ciro didn’t come out. I wait for Ciro to come out because every night he gives me a slice. Last night he didn’t.
He adjusts the umbrellas on his shoulder.
Who closed the shutter in the night?
The man with the silver ring. He came last month; Ciro turned him away at the door, everyone saw. But last night that man wasn’t here. I know this street; if that man came, I’d know.
Who in the neighbourhood had a problem with Ciro?

On the morning of 6 October 2030, at a pizzeria in Forcella, the master and owner Ciro Amato (47) was found dead in the cold room behind the kitchen.

His partner Enzo Ferraro found the body at 06.40 when he opened the shutter. The victim’s wife Rosaria Amato said her husband had not come home in the night. The waitress Lucia Bianco was working the evening shift. The Senegalese street vendor Moussa Diop sets up his stall outside the shop every night.
INCIDENT REPORT
Request the autopsy report
Request permission to search Enzo Ferraro’s car
Request an examination of the cold room
Request an examination of the till ledger
The neighbourhood’s ‘friend’.
I’m a friend, that’s all.
Rocco Greco — interview

Ciro was stubborn. A flour matter, a business matter. I don’t lock anyone in a cold room; last night I was on Ischia, at a wedding, a hundred people saw me. But Enzo… Enzo owes me. I’ll tell you that too, call it my gift to you.
He turns the ring on his little finger.
Ciro Amato turned you away at the door.
The victim’s wife.
Ciro kept the till ledger. Last month he said, ‘Enzo’s taking from the till, Rosaria; your brother is paying his gambling debts out of our bakery.’ I didn’t want to believe it.
How was the shop doing for money?
I won’t talk about anyone but Ciro.
I called at one in the morning; his phone was off. I called Enzo; he said, ‘Ciro’s left, gone to a bar I expect.’ Enzo is my brother. I thought he wouldn’t lie.
She turns a button on her cardigan.
What did you do when your husband didn’t come home?
Rosaria Amato — interview
Vico dei Panettieri, the camera of the shop opposite the pizzeria. 5 October 23.00 – 6 October 01.00.
STREET CAMERA — log transcript

The street vendor saw who lowered the shutter; the street camera confirmed it. The waitress gave the argument, the widow the withdrawals from the till. A justified search found the handle in the glovebox. The collector’s wedding on Ischia cleared him but gave Enzo away.
In Napoli even the flour arrives in someone’s name.
Forcella — October 2030

Enzo Ferraro owed the neighbourhood collector €12,000 in gambling debts; the debt would be wiped if the pizzeria switched to Caruso flour. When his partner and brother-in-law Ciro refused, Enzo lowered the shutter at night and went back inside, struck Ciro on the back of the neck, carried him into the cold room, removed the inside handle and turned the thermostat to -18.
Who killed Ciro Amato?
